facts.statement: Turiasaurus had a skull measuring 70 centimetres in length, which paleontologists consider relatively small for its size.
facts.quote: The length of its skull is 70 centimetres, which is not too large.

facts.statement: The femur of Turiasaurus measured approximately 2.2 meters in length.
facts.quote: Its femur was some 2.2 m in length.

facts.statement: Early estimates based on a 1.79-meter humerus and other bones suggested Turiasaurus reached 36 to 38 meters in length and weighed between 39.9 and 47.36 tonnes.
facts.quote: El estudio de un húmero de 1,79 metros de longitud y de otros huesos de su esqueleto ha permitido estimar una longitud de entre 36 y 38 metros y un peso de entre 39,9 y 47,36 toneladas.

facts.statement: More recent estimates suggest Turiasaurus was 21 to 30 meters long and weighed between 30 and 50 tonnes.
facts.quote: Estimaciones más recientes sugieren una longitud de 21 a 30 metros de largo, pero un peso comparable de 30 a 50 toneladas.

facts.statement: The first remains of Turiasaurus were discovered on May 23, 2003, at El Húmero, just one kilometer from the town of Riodeva in the province of Teruel, Spain.
facts.quote: Los primeros restos de Turiasaurus aparecieron el 23 de mayo de 2003 en el paraje de El Húmero, apenas a un kilómetro del pueblo de Riodeva, en la provincia de Teruel.

facts.statement: The type species Turiasaurus riodevensis was formally described by Royo-Torres, Cobos, and Alcalá in 2006.
facts.quote: La especie tipo fue formalmente descrita por Royo-Torres, Cobos & Alcala, en 2006.

facts.statement: The genus name Turiasaurus is derived from the Turia River in Teruel and the Greek word 'sauros,' meaning lizard.
facts.quote: El nombre del género deriva de Turia, nombre de un río de Teruel (en cuya provincia se le llama Guadalaviar, pueblo donde nace), y del término griego sauros, que significa lagarto.

facts.statement: The species name 'riodevensis' refers to Riodeva, the locality where the first remains of the species were found.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie hace alusión a Riodeva, localidad donde se encontraron los primeros restos de la especie.

facts.statement: The skull of Turiasaurus was formally described in 2012.
facts.quote: En 2012 se ha descrito el cráneo.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Luis Alcalá hypothesized that Turiasaurus had a relatively small head because a larger one might have caused the animal to break its neck.
facts.quote: According to the paleontologist Luis Alcalá, this is because a larger head might have caused Turiasaurus to break its neck.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Turiasaurus outside the Neosauropoda division within a new clade called Turiasauria, alongside Losillasaurus and Galvesaurus.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic analysis shows that Turiasaurus lies outside of the Neosauropoda division and belongs to a new clade, Turiasauria, together with Losillasaurus and Galvesaurus.

facts.statement: Turiasaurus is the first giant sauropod identified in the Turiasauria clade, whereas other large sauropods like Diplodocus, Brachiosaurus, and Argentinosaurus belong to the Neosauropoda clade.
facts.quote: Es el primer saurópodo gigante que pertenece a este grupo, ya que las otras especies de gran porte, como Diplodocus, Brachiosaurus y Argentinosaurus pertenecen al clado de los neosaurópodos.

facts.statement: Turiasaurus riodevensis lived during the Kimmeridgian stage of the Late Jurassic and is known from fossils found in the Villar del Arzobispo Formation of Teruel, Spain.
facts.quote: It is known from a multiple fossil specimens representing the species Turiasaurus riodevensis, found in the Kimmeridgian Villar del Arzobispo Formation of Teruel, Spain.

facts.statement: Turiasaurus lived during the Late Jurassic, approximately 155 to 146 million years ago, spanning from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian stages in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió entre finales del período Jurásico , hace aproximadamente entre 155 y 146 millones de años, desde el Kimmeridgiense al Titoniense, en lo que hoy es Europa.

facts.statement: Approximately 150 million years ago, the habitat of Turiasaurus was an extensive tidal plain cut by large rivers flowing into the Tethys Sea.
facts.quote: Hace 150 millones de años la zona donde se encontraron los restos era una extensa llanura sometida a la inﬂuencia de las mareas y surcada por ríos caudalosos que desembocaban en el mar de Tethys.

facts.statement: Fossils found in nearby deposits of similar age include a diplodocid sauropod, a stegosaurian, an unclassified ornithopod, crocodiles, turtles, and fish.
facts.quote: En yacimientos cercanos de edad similar se han encontrado restos de una especie de saurópodo diplodócido, un estegosáurido y un ornitópodo aún sin clasificar, así como restos de cocodrilos, tortugas y peces.

facts.statement: Turiasaurus is considered the largest dinosaur ever discovered in Europe and ranks among the largest dinosaurs known globally.
facts.quote: It is believed to be the largest dinosaur ever found in Europe, and is among the largest dinosaurs known.

facts.statement: The new specimen found in Riodeva was named Turiasaurus riodevensis.
facts.quote: El nuevo espécimen fue nombrado como Turiasaurus riodevensis.
